zh.summary: 從查詢身分、Base、Scope、欄位與分頁完成狀態判讀 LDAP 列舉，並用完整 LDAP／Kerberos 入門串起目錄、票證與授權。

sourceBody.text: 這一課的核心問題是：
當你使用工具查詢一間公司的帳號資料，結果顯示有 2 個人，你能不能因此斷定，這間公司只有 2 個帳號？
答案是：不行。
因為你看到的結果，取決於你從哪裡查、用誰的身分查、設定什麼條件，以及查詢是否真的完成。
這是 CEH（Certified Ethical Hacker）M04 Enumeration（列舉）非常重要的觀念，同時也是 Windows Server、企業網路管理、Active Directory（AD）和資安稽核的基礎。
本課以合成企業情境解釋協定原理與 CEH 判讀方法，並以文末的一手規範核對技術界線。
一、先把 LDAP 想成公司的員工資料庫
假設有一家公司，員工有 500 人，分成研發部、人事部、財務部等單位。
人事部有一份員工名冊，記錄每個人的姓名、帳號、電子郵件、部門以及所屬群組。

visual.caption: 圖 1｜公司員工目錄
visual.description: 連線表示目錄的隸屬關係，三個部門彼此平行；真實目錄還可能包含子部門、電腦、群組和多個網域。

sourceBody.text: 現在你走到公司人事部櫃檯，問：
「請問研發部有哪些員工？」
櫃檯回答：「小林、小陳。」
你可能會認為研發部只有兩個人。但實際上，還可能有以下情況：

items: 櫃檯只查了研發部的直屬員工，沒有查下面的子部門。
你的身分只能查看部分員工資料。
系統每次最多顯示兩筆，後面還有更多。
櫃檯依照你設定的條件，只找出某一類員工。

sourceBody.text: 所以，查到兩筆資料，不等於整個資料庫只有兩筆。
這就是本課最重要的邏輯。
二、LDAP 和 Active Directory 到底是什麼？
這兩個名詞經常一起出現，但不是同一件事。

rows: 查詢員工名冊的溝通語言
告訴目錄系統要查什麼
企業的集中式帳號與目錄管理系統
管理使用者、群組、電腦及相關目錄資訊
提供網域身分驗證及目錄服務的伺服器
處理相關驗證及目錄請求
盤點指定範圍內可見的帳號、群組等資訊

sourceBody.text: 例如，一位員工登入公司 Windows 電腦時，電腦可能需要透過網域控制站完成身分驗證；公司管理員也可能利用 LDAP 查詢某位員工所屬的群組。
但要注意：AD 不只使用 LDAP。 在 Windows 網域環境中，Kerberos、DNS 等技術同樣重要。
用一句話區分：
AD 是管理資料與身分的系統，LDAP 是存取目錄資料的協定。
三、先看懂目錄的結構：DN、OU、CN、DC
LDAP 的資料不是像 Excel 那樣，單純把所有員工放在一張表裡，而是有階層結構。
假設你看到：
CN=Lin,OU=People,DC=example,DC=test
這就是 Distinguished Name（DN），可以把它理解成「員工資料在目錄中的完整地址」。

rows: 這筆資料的名稱，例如 Lin
整筆資料在目錄中的識別路徑

sourceBody.text: 這串 DN 就像告訴你：
「請到 example.test 公司目錄的 People 單位，找 Lin 這筆資料。」
要小心：DC=example 的 DC 是 Domain Component，不是前面提到的 Domain Controller。兩者剛好縮寫相同。
四、Base、Scope、Filter、Attributes：LDAP 查詢的四大設定
這一節是本課最需要理解的地方。
假設你正在幫公司盤點帳號。你必須先告訴查詢系統：「從哪裡開始、查到多深、找什麼人，以及想看哪些資料。」

visual.caption: 圖 2｜一次 LDAP 查詢的四個問題
visual.description: 四個設定共同界定查詢，並列卡片不表示執行先後。

items.title: 01 · Base
items.body: 從哪裡開始查？例如 People 單位。

items.title: 02 · Scope
items.body: 往下查幾層？只查直屬或包含所有子層。

items.title: 03 · Filter
items.body: 找符合什麼條件的人？例如只找使用者帳號。

items.title: 04 · Attributes
items.body: 要讀取哪些欄位？例如姓名、電子郵件。

sourceBody.text: 其中 Scope（搜尋範圍）又分成三種。

rows: 只檢查指定的那個項目
不包含起點及更深子層

sourceBody.text: 這是 LDAP 標準搜尋模型，也是 Microsoft AD 查詢 API 所採用的基本概念。
用同一棵目錄比較三種 Scope

visual.caption: 圖 3｜同一棵目錄的三種搜尋深度
visual.description: 連線只表示父子關係。綠框為 one-level 的候選：Lin、Chen、研發小組；尚未套用 Filter 或權限。base 只查 People；subtree 包含六個項目，不能自動跨到其他網域。

items.title: People
items.body: 查詢起點；base 的唯一候選

items.title: 研發小組
items.body: People 的直接子項目；另有子項目

sourceBody.text: 這裡就能發現一個重要陷阱：
假設公司有 500 個使用者，你使用 one-level 只查到 20 人，就不能說公司只有 20 人。因為其他員工可能藏在下一層的子部門。
另外，即使使用 subtree，也不代表一定查完整個公司的所有網域。Subtree 只能保證從你指定的 Base 往下搜尋，不會自動涵蓋整個 AD 樹系。
五、RootDSE 和 Global Catalog：為什麼有不同查詢入口？
想像一家跨國企業，在台灣、美國、日本分別有員工管理系統。
你向台灣的管理員詢問，得到的資料不一定包含美國、日本的全部員工。
AD 也有類似問題。
RootDSE：伺服器的服務說明牌
RootDSE 是 LDAP 伺服器提供自身資訊的特殊項目。
你可以透過它了解伺服器支援哪些功能，以及目錄的相關入口。
例如 defaultNamingContext 可以幫你知道預設網域的查詢起點。
但讀到 RootDSE 不代表有權限讀取所有員工帳號，也不代表取得了完整的 AD 地圖。
Global Catalog（GC）：跨網域的索引
GC 可以理解為一份跨網域的索引，讓你不用每次都先知道資料位於哪個網域。
但它有一個重要限制：GC 對其他網域通常保留每個物件的部分屬性，不是所有欄位的完整副本。
所以查 GC 時沒有看到某個欄位，未必表示原始目錄沒有這個資料。
六、LDAP Bind、權限與 TLS：登入成功不代表什麼都能查
假設你拿公司員工證進入辦公大樓。
門禁確認你是員工，並不代表你可以進入董事長辦公室、機房或財務室。
LDAP 也要分清楚三種不同問題。

rows: 目前採用何種驗證身分
可存取哪些物件或欄位
有沒有提供加密、完整性與伺服器身分驗證等保護

sourceBody.text: LDAP 的 Bind 與身分驗證狀態有關。即使 Bind 成功，也不能推論目前身分可以讀取所有資料。
另外，LDAP 的傳輸安全常見下列方式。

rows: 協定本身不代表已加密
在 LDAP 連線上協商啟動 TLS
為適用的非 TLS SASL 連線提供訊息完整性及來源驗證

sourceBody.text: LDAP Signing 不等於加密。
簽章比較像防止文件被偷偷修改；加密則是讓傳輸內容不容易被旁人看懂。TLS 可提供機密性、完整性和伺服器身分驗證，但必須正確建立 TLS 連線並驗證憑證。
而在 Microsoft AD 中，LDAP Signing 主要適用於非 TLS 的 SASL 工作階段，不應誤認它是所有 LDAP 連線都額外套用的獨立保護。
七、最重要的案例：sizeLimitExceeded 是什麼？
回到正式教材的情境。
你被授權查詢公司 People 單位的帳號，工具顯示：

visual.caption: 圖 4｜LDAP Search Result：未完整取得結果
visual.description: 教學合成資料。收到兩筆只證明本次可見結果；代碼 4 表示達到筆數限制，不能推論目錄只有兩人。只要求 cn，也不能推論沒有 mail。

sourceBody.text: sizeLimitExceeded 的意思是：「這次搜尋達到筆數限制，沒有正常收完。」
RFC 4511 確實定義了 success = 0、timeLimitExceeded = 3、sizeLimitExceeded = 4 等結果代碼。
因此，你目前只能確認：這次查詢取得了兩筆資料，但完整數量尚未確定。
更重要的是，因為你只要求回傳 cn，所以沒有電子郵件欄位並不能證明員工沒有電子郵件。
那要怎麼把後面的資料查出來？
當伺服器支援且查詢條件允許時，可以使用 Paging（分頁搜尋）。分頁大小與整次查詢的 sizeLimit 是不同設定；不能把同一個總筆數限制原封不動保留，再假定分頁會自動繞過它。
想像有一本 500 頁的名冊，一次只允許印出 100 頁。你就要分五次取回，並且確認有沒有全部收到。
LDAP 的分頁搜尋可以透過伺服器提供的續查資訊（cookie）讀取下一批資料。每次都要檢查結果狀態，並確認最後收到空 cookie 才能判定該分頁序列結束；中斷、錯誤或遺失續查資訊都要記錄。

visual.caption: 圖 5｜分批取得結果並確認結束
visual.description: 箭頭表示分頁續查，不代表提升權限或擴大範圍。每頁 100 筆只是示例；檢查結果代碼與最後的空 cookie，總數仍須依實際回傳計算。

items.title: 第 1 頁
items.body: 取得 100 筆，保留伺服器續查 cookie。

items.title: 第 2 頁
items.body: 帶回前頁 cookie，再取一批；示例為 100 筆。

items.title: 後續頁面
items.body: 逐批核對狀態，直到最後收到空 cookie。

sourceBody.text: 但分頁只解決「資料分批取回」的問題，不會提升查詢者的權限，也不會自動擴大搜尋範圍。
這裡還要記住一句話：
success 代表這次 LDAP 操作成功完成，不代表你已經完成整個公司的帳號盤點。
八、從 CEH 的觀點，為什麼需要學這個？
在 CEH M04 Enumeration 中，最重要的是學會「根據服務回應判斷資訊暴露與可見範圍」。
假設你正在執行一項經過授權的企業資安評估。你發現某個低權限帳號能夠查詢員工姓名、群組與組織架構。
這時你要思考的不是單純「我查到幾個帳號」，而是：
這些資訊是否原本就預期讓該帳號讀取？會不會暴露超出業務需要的資訊？目前看到的結果是否完整？又有哪些資料根本沒有被查詢？
在防守方的角度，應該記錄查詢身分、伺服器、時間、Base、Scope、Filter、Attributes、結果代碼及分頁完成狀態，並以最小權限控制資料可見範圍。
而且，看到大量 LDAP 查詢也不能直接判定正在遭受攻擊。合法的資產盤點與目錄同步服務，也可能產生大量查詢。
最後整理：判斷 LDAP 查詢是否完整的六問框架

headers: 如果沒確認，可能誤判什麼？
rows: 以為低權限看到的就是全部
把某單位誤當整個網域
4. Filter 與 Attributes 是什麼？
漏掉符合其他條件的人或欄位
5. 結果代碼與分頁狀態如何？
把未完成的結果當成完整
6. 是否涵蓋所有必要目錄與網域？
以為單一網域等於整間公司

sourceBody.text: 這套邏輯不只適用於 LDAP，也能應用在其他服務列舉、API 分頁、資料庫查詢及資產盤點：先界定觀察範圍，再判斷證據支持什麼結論。
理解測驗｜CEH M04-08
假設你是一位受委託的資安稽核人員，正在盤點企業的 AD 帳號。
你使用已驗證的低權限帳號，經過有效的 TLS 連線執行 LDAP 查詢：
查詢紀錄

Base: OU=People,DC=example,DC=test
Scope: one-level
Attributes: cn
Result: 20 entries
Result Code: success (0)
同事看完後說：「我們已經確認 People 單位及所有子部門總共只有 20 個人，而且這些人都沒有電子郵件。」
請你回答三個問題：
Q1. 同事的結論有哪些地方不正確？
Q2. 如果要查詢 People 單位下所有子部門的員工，應優先調整哪一個查詢設定？
Q3. 既然結果顯示 success (0)，為什麼仍然不能保證這 20 筆就是全部？

paragraphs: Q1：one-level 只涵蓋 People 的直接下一層，不包含 People 本身與更深子部門。cn 是唯一要求回傳的欄位，沒有 mail 不能證明員工沒有電子郵件。20 筆是目前身分與查詢條件下的結果，不能當成整個單位所有人的總數。
Q2：優先把 Scope 改為 subtree，保留正確的 Base，並核對 Filter、所需 Attributes、身分可見性與所有必要目錄。subtree 包含起點及所有後代，但不自動涵蓋其他網域。
Q3：success (0) 只證明本次操作在指定條件下成功完成。盤點完整性還要核對身分、Base、Scope、Filter、Attributes、筆數／時間限制、分頁最後的空 cookie，以及是否涵蓋所有必要目錄與網域。有效 TLS 保護傳輸，不會提升讀取權限。

sourceBody.text: 補充 A｜LDAP 是什麼？從零開始的白話教學
LDAP 可以把它想成「公司查詢員工名冊的一套標準溝通方法」。
假設一家公司有 3,000 名員工，每個人都有電腦帳號、密碼、電子郵件、部門和不同的系統權限。
公司不可能要求每套系統都自己維護一份員工資料。否則員工一離職，IT 人員可能要去十幾套系統刪除他的帳號。
因此，公司會建立集中式的「目錄服務」（Directory Service），而 LDAP 就是讓其他軟體可以跟這個目錄服務溝通的協定。
一、先從一間公司的實際情況理解
假設有一家「Kairos 科技公司」。

visual.caption: 圖 6｜公司中央員工目錄
visual.description: 連線表示共同使用中央目錄，不表示每次登入必經 LDAP。各系統可查詢目錄；登入與授權也可能使用 Kerberos 等其他協定。

items.title: 公司中央員工目錄
items.body: 記錄帳號、姓名、部門、群組等資訊

sourceBody.text: 現在有位員工叫小明。
小明打開公司內部系統，輸入帳號 ming 和密碼。
這套系統不一定自己保存小明的密碼，而是可能透過 LDAP 與中央目錄服務確認身分。
系統可以詢問：

items: 有沒有 ming 這個帳號？
他是不是合法的使用者？
他屬於哪個部門？
他是不是管理員群組的成員？

sourceBody.text: 中央目錄依照驗證方式、權限和查詢條件回應，系統再決定小明能否進入以及能使用哪些功能。
這樣就能集中管理員工帳號，而不是每套軟體都重做一次。
二、LDAP 的英文全名是什麼？
LDAP = Lightweight Directory Access Protocol
拆開來看：

rows: 相對早期 X.500 目錄存取方式較簡化
像一本有組織的員工電話簿
查詢、讀取，或在授權下修改資料
雙方講話都遵守的共同規則

sourceBody.text: 這裡有個非常重要的觀念：
LDAP 本身不是一套資料庫，也不是一台伺服器，而是一種通訊協定。
這是 IETF RFC 4511 與 Microsoft LDAP 文件中的基本定位。
三、LDAP、Active Directory、Domain Controller 有什麼不同？
這三個名詞最容易搞混。
我們把它們想成一間公司的行政系統。

rows: 向人事部詢問資料的標準語言
公司的人事與帳號管理體系
提供 AD 網域服務的伺服器
實際提供服務的人事辦公室

sourceBody.text: 例如，Windows Server 可以部署 Active Directory Domain Services（AD DS）。其他應用程式可以透過 LDAP 查詢其目錄資訊。
但 AD 並不只有 LDAP，還會運用 Kerberos、DNS、Group Policy 等技術。
而 LDAP 也不是只能搭配 Microsoft AD。OpenLDAP 等其他目錄服務同樣支援 LDAP。
四、LDAP 裡面的資料長什麼樣？
假設公司保存小明的資料。

visual.caption: 圖 7｜員工資料：小明
visual.description: 簡化的通用 LDAP Entry（目錄項目）。不同目錄的帳號屬性可能不同，例如 AD 常使用 sAMAccountName；ou 欄位不取代 DN 的位置識別。

sourceBody.text: LDAP 會用 DN（Distinguished Name）表示一筆資料在目錄中的位置。
例如：
cn=Ming,ou=People,dc=example,dc=test
這串文字可以這樣讀：

items: cn=Ming：找 Ming 這個項目。
ou=People：它位於 People 組織單位。
dc=example,dc=test：所屬的網域目錄是 example.test。

sourceBody.text: 你可以把 DN 想成一個人的完整地址，不只是他的姓名。
五、一次 LDAP 查詢是怎麼發生的？
假設公司管理員想知道研發部有哪些員工。

visual.caption: 圖 8｜一次 LDAP 查詢如何發生
visual.description: 箭頭表示這個查詢的處理順序。回傳內容與查詢狀態要一起判讀，不能把成功回應當成全部資料可見。

items.title: 2 · 送出 LDAP Search
items.body: 指定搜尋位置、範圍與條件。

items.title: 3 · 目錄伺服器
items.body: 根據條件與存取權限查詢資料。

items.title: 4 · 回傳結果
items.body: 小明、小華、小美……以及查詢狀態。

sourceBody.text: LDAP Search 有四個基本觀念：
例如 LDAP 的篩選條件：
(cn=Ming)
意思是：找出 cn 等於 Ming 的目錄項目。
再例如：
(mail=*)
意思是：找出有 mail 屬性的項目。
在正式環境中，LDAP 還有 Bind（建立驗證身分）、Modify（修改）、Add（新增）等操作；具體能否執行取決於伺服器與權限設定。
六、LDAP 安全嗎？為什麼 CEH 需要學它？
LDAP 本身不保證傳輸已加密，因此安全設定很重要。

rows: 不能只因使用 LDAP 就認為資料已加密
在既有連線上協商 TLS
一開始就建立 TLS 保護

sourceBody.text: 使用 TLS 時，也需要正確驗證伺服器憑證，才不會錯誤地信任冒充的伺服器。Microsoft 也建議使用適當的 TLS 或 SASL 保護 LDAP 通訊。
從 CEH（道德駭客）角度，LDAP 很值得學，因為企業目錄可能記錄大量組織資訊。若權限設定不當，未經授權的人可能取得本不應開放的帳號與群組資訊。
但要記得：
查得到某個帳號，不代表知道他的密碼；能成功登入 LDAP，也不代表擁有管理員權限。
七、最後用四個問題整理

items: LDAP 是什麼？ 一套讓軟體存取目錄服務的通訊協定。
LDAP 用來做什麼？ 查詢帳號、群組、組織資料，並支援身分驗證及授權管理的相關流程。
LDAP 和 AD 一樣嗎？ 不一樣。LDAP 是協定，AD 是微軟的目錄與身分管理技術。
LDAP 是不是安全的？ 取決於驗證、存取權限及傳輸保護等設定。

sourceBody.text: 小測驗：確認你是否真的理解
1. 一間公司使用 Active Directory 管理員工帳號。另一套內部系統需要查詢員工資料，通常可以使用什麼協定？
LDAP
HDMI
USB
2. 如果 LDAP 查詢找到小明的帳號，代表什麼？
已經取得小明的密碼
確認查詢範圍內有符合條件且可見的帳號資料
已取得公司管理員權限
3. LDAP 與 Active Directory 的關係，哪個比較正確？
兩者是完全相同的產品
LDAP 是協定；AD 是可支援 LDAP 的目錄管理系統
LDAP 只能在 Windows 使用

paragraphs: 第 1 題：LDAP。LDAP 是目錄存取協定；HDMI 與 USB 是不同用途的介面，不能據此查詢 AD 目錄。
第 2 題：確認查詢範圍內有符合條件且可見的帳號資料。這不提供密碼，也不授予管理員權限。
第 3 題：LDAP 是協定；AD 是可支援 LDAP 的目錄管理系統。兩者不是同一產品，OpenLDAP 等系統也可使用 LDAP。

sourceBody.text: 學完 LDAP 後，下一個最有價值的主題是 Active Directory 如何利用 LDAP、Kerberos 和 DNS 共同完成企業帳號登入與權限管理。這能把 CEH 的列舉知識與真正的 Windows 網路工程串在一起。
補充 B｜Kerberos 是什麼？從零開始的白話教學
Kerberos 是一種「身分驗證協定」（Authentication Protocol）。它最重要的特色是：透過加密票證（Ticket），讓你不必每次存取公司系統都重新輸入密碼。
你可以把 Kerberos 想成「公司的中央門禁與通行證制度」。
前面學過的 LDAP 是用來查詢公司員工名冊；Kerberos 則是用來證明「你確實是某位員工」。
先記住兩句話：

items: LDAP：查詢你是誰、屬於哪個部門。
Kerberos：使用加密票證證明你的身分。

sourceBody.text: 兩者經常一起出現在 Active Directory（AD）環境，但負責不同工作。
一、為什麼公司需要 Kerberos？
假設 Kairos 科技公司有 3,000 名員工，每個人每天需要使用許多系統。

visual.caption: 圖 9｜每套系統都要重新輸入密碼嗎？
visual.description: 員工小明上午 9:00 登入公司電腦。三個服務彼此平行；只有適當整合 Kerberos 的系統才能減少重複登入，服務仍各自檢查授權。

items.title: 員工小明
items.body: 上午 9:00 登入公司電腦

sourceBody.text: 傳統上，如果每套系統各自處理帳號和密碼，就可能造成大量重複驗證與密碼管理問題。
Kerberos 提供另一個方式：第一次登入時，先向可信任的中央驗證服務證明身分，取得一張可以用來申請其他票證的憑證。之後要存取不同服務，再取得相應的服務票證。
這也是它能支援 Single Sign-On（SSO，單一登入）的原因。
二、用「遊樂園通行證」理解 Kerberos
假設你去一座大型遊樂園。
遊樂園有三個區域：雲霄飛車、海盜船和水族館。
你的入園流程可以分成三個階段。
第一階段：先證明你是合法遊客
你到入口驗證身分，工作人員發給你一張「可以申請各區門票的通行證」。
這張通行證就像 Kerberos 的 TGT（Ticket-Granting Ticket）。
第二階段：取得指定設施的門票
你想搭雲霄飛車，就拿通行證到票務中心，申請一張雲霄飛車專用的門票。
這張門票就是 Service Ticket（服務票證）。
第三階段：進入指定設施
你到雲霄飛車入口，出示專用門票。工作人員確認票證有效後，再依照設施規定決定是否讓你搭乘。
這就像目標服務驗證 Kerberos 票證，並進一步檢查存取權限。
最關鍵的是：你不必每次都回入口重新證明身分，但也不是拿到通行證就能自由進入所有區域。
TGT 用來申請服務票證；Service Ticket 則用來向特定服務證明身分。
三、Kerberos 真正的運作原理
Kerberos 主要涉及三個角色。
在 Windows Active Directory 環境中，KDC 通常執行於 Domain Controller（DC，網域控制站）。
KDC 內部又分為兩個邏輯功能：AS（Authentication Service）負責核發 TGT，TGS（Ticket-Granting Service）負責核發服務票證。它們不一定是兩台不同的電腦。

visual.caption: 圖 10｜Kerberos 的三階段票證流程
visual.description: 前兩階段箭頭分別表示請求與回覆；第三階段出示票證後由服務檢查授權，「依權限存取」不是固定的 AP 回覆封包。若要求雙向驗證，服務可回傳 AP_REP。AS／TGS 是 KDC 的邏輯功能；省略預先驗證往返、金鑰細節及快取重用。

items.title: 小明的電腦 → KDC / AS
items.body:
階段 1 · AS Exchange
請求初始票證並證明身分
取得 TGT

items.title: 小明的電腦 → KDC / TGS
items.body:
階段 2 · TGS Exchange
使用 TGT 申請檔案伺服器票證
取得 Service Ticket

items.title: 小明的電腦 → 檔案伺服器
items.body:
階段 3 · AP Exchange
出示服務票證與 Authenticator
驗證成功後，依權限存取

sourceBody.text: 這個流程是 Kerberos V5 的基本設計，定義於 [IETF RFC 4120](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4120.html)。
那麼，加密到底發生在哪裡？
Kerberos 並不是把密碼直接交給所有伺服器。
以常見的密碼式驗證來說：

items: 小明的電腦使用密碼衍生出的金鑰，證明自己掌握正確的驗證資訊。
KDC 驗證後，核發加密的 TGT 與對應的工作階段金鑰資訊。
小明需要存取檔案伺服器時，用 TGT 向 KDC 申請服務票證。
KDC 核發由目標服務可驗證的加密票證。
檔案伺服器檢查票證及相關驗證資訊。

sourceBody.text: 因此，在標準密碼式 Kerberos 流程中，使用者的明文密碼不需要直接在網路上傳送給服務伺服器。
而且票證還有有效期限、加密保護與防止重播的驗證機制。
不過，Kerberos 主要負責身分驗證，不能因此認為所有後續應用資料都自動加密。資料傳輸是否受到保護，仍取決於應用協定，例如 HTTPS、SMB 加密或其他安全設定。
四、為什麼 Kerberos 很在意電腦時間？
這是資訊工程和 CEH 特別重要的知識。
假設小明的電腦時間是上午 9:00，但公司的 Domain Controller 認為現在是上午 9:20。
Kerberos 使用時間戳記來協助抵抗重播攻擊（Replay Attack）。
如果時間差距太大，伺服器可能拒絕驗證，因為它無法信任驗證資訊的時間有效性。
在一般 Windows AD 設定中，預設允許的時間偏差通常是 5 分鐘，而且可以依政策調整。
這也解釋了為什麼企業網路很重視 NTP（Network Time Protocol）與 Windows 時間同步服務。
你在 CEH M04 學習 NTP 列舉時，可以將兩者連在一起理解：時間同步不只是讓電腦時鐘準確，它也可能直接影響身分驗證的可靠性。
五、LDAP、Kerberos、Active Directory、DNS 如何一起運作？
這四者的分工可以用一張表串起來。

rows: 查詢使用者、群組及其他目錄資訊
利用加密票證進行驗證
誰來管理這些身分與目錄？
提供網域帳號、目錄與管理機制

sourceBody.text: 舉個例子：
當小明登入公司 Windows 網域電腦，並且打開共用資料夾時，DNS 可協助找到網域服務或目標主機；Kerberos 可以完成身分驗證；AD 提供相關帳號和群組資訊；目標檔案伺服器再依權限決定能否讀取檔案。
LDAP 可能用於目錄查詢，但不是每次 Windows 網域登入都必須由用戶端直接發出 LDAP 查詢。
六、從 CEH 角度，Kerberos 有哪些安全風險？
Kerberos 是成熟的身分驗證協定，但不代表它不會被攻擊。

rows: 偷走可用票證後，冒用票證持有者
保護端點、憑證與票證儲存環境
利用某些服務票證，嘗試離線猜測弱服務帳號密碼
強密碼、gMSA、適當加密演算法
在取得高度敏感的 Kerberos 金鑰後，偽造 TGT
嚴格保護網域控制站與 KRBTGT 金鑰
重送截取到的驗證訊息
時間戳記、Authenticator 與重播檢查

sourceBody.text: 這些名稱不需要一次全部背起來。先記住安全邏輯：
Kerberos 降低了每次傳送密碼的需求，但如果端點、票證或核心金鑰被竊取，仍然可能發生身分冒用。
在 Windows 網域稽核中，事件 ID 4768 可以用來觀察 TGT 申請，4769 則與服務票證申請有關。這些紀錄可協助辨識異常驗證活動，但單一事件本身不能直接證明遭到攻擊。
七、你可以在 Windows 電腦上看到 Kerberos 票證嗎？
可以。在你有權操作的 Windows 環境中，開啟 PowerShell 或命令提示字元：
klist
若你使用的是有 Kerberos 票證的登入工作階段，這個指令可以列出目前快取中的票證資訊，例如票證對應的服務、有效起訖時間等。
如果沒有看到票證，不一定代表 Kerberos 壞掉；也可能是目前使用本機帳號、尚未存取需要 Kerberos 的服務，或該工作階段使用其他驗證方式。
這個指令只是讀取資訊，不會主動修改網域設定。
八、三個觀念，確認你真的學會 Kerberos
1. 小明登入公司電腦後，想要存取檔案伺服器。Kerberos 通常會讓他先使用什麼來申請服務票證？
TGT
LDAP 查詢結果
IP 位址
2. 小明已經通過 Kerberos 驗證，是否代表他能讀取公司所有機密檔案？
是，驗證成功就擁有全部權限
否，仍需由目標服務檢查授權
3. 電腦與 Domain Controller 的時間相差 20 分鐘，可能造成什麼問題？
Kerberos 可能因時間偏差而拒絕驗證
LDAP 會自動刪除使用者
所有服務票證永久有效

paragraphs: 第 1 題：TGT。用戶端使用 TGT 向 KDC 的 TGS 申請指定服務的票證；LDAP 查詢結果與 IP 位址不能取代它。
第 2 題：否，仍需由目標服務檢查授權。驗證身分與准許讀取某個檔案是不同判斷。
第 3 題：Kerberos 可能因時間偏差而拒絕驗證。20 分鐘超過常見的 5 分鐘預設容許值，但仍須核對實際政策；不會因此自動刪除 LDAP 使用者，也不會讓票證永久有效。

sourceBody.text: 本課最重要的結論：Kerberos 不負責決定你能看哪些機密資料，而是讓系統能夠安全地驗證「你是誰」。
接下來最值得深入的是 Kerberos 的兩種票證——TGT 與 Service Ticket——以及為什麼知道密碼、持有票證、擁有系統權限，是三件不同的事。
一手來源與適用範圍

en.summary: Interpret LDAP enumeration through identity, Base, Scope, attributes, and paging completion, with complete LDAP and Kerberos introductions connecting directories, tickets, and authorization.

sourceBody.text: This lesson asks a central question:
If a tool querying a company's accounts returns 2 people, can you conclude that the company has only 2 accounts?
No.
What you see depends on where you search, which identity you use, the conditions you specify, and whether the search actually finishes.
This is a core idea in CEH (Certified Ethical Hacker) M04 Enumeration and a foundation for Windows Server, enterprise network administration, Active Directory (AD), and security audits.
The lesson uses synthetic enterprise scenarios to explain protocol mechanisms and CEH interpretation, with technical boundaries checked against the primary references at the end.
1. Think of a directory as a company's employee register
Imagine a company with 500 employees across Engineering, Human Resources, Finance, and other departments.
HR maintains a register of names, accounts, email addresses, departments, and group memberships.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | Company employee directory
visual.description: Lines indicate directory containment; the three departments are peers. Real directories may include subdepartments, computers, groups, and multiple domains.

sourceBody.text: You walk up to the HR desk and ask:
“Who works in Engineering?”
The desk replies: “Lin and Chen.”
You might infer that Engineering has only two people. Several other explanations are possible:

items: The desk checked only direct members, leaving out people in subdepartments.
Your identity can view only some employee records.
The system displays at most two records at a time, with more still to retrieve.
Your conditions select only a particular type of employee.

sourceBody.text: Finding two records therefore does not establish that the entire directory contains only two.
That distinction guides the rest of the lesson.
2. What are LDAP and Active Directory?
These terms often appear together, but name different things.

rows: A language for querying the employee register
Tell a directory what information to retrieve
A centralized enterprise account and directory system
Manage users, groups, computers, and related directory information
A server providing domain authentication and directory services
Collecting and organizing information under stated conditions
Inventory visible accounts, groups, and other information within a defined scope

sourceBody.text: For example, when an employee signs in to a company Windows computer, it may authenticate through a domain controller. An administrator may also use LDAP to query the employee's group memberships.
AD uses more than LDAP. Kerberos and DNS also play important roles in Windows domains.
A concise distinction is:
AD manages directory data and identities; LDAP is a protocol for accessing directory data.
3. Read the directory structure: DN, OU, CN, and DC
Directory data has a hierarchy, rather than simply putting every employee into one spreadsheet table.
Suppose you see:
CN=Lin,OU=People,DC=example,DC=test
This is a Distinguished Name (DN). Think of it as the complete address of an employee record in the directory.

rows: The entry's name, such as Lin
An organizational container, such as People
A component of a domain name
The identifying path of the complete entry

sourceBody.text: Read the DN as:
“In the example.test directory, open the People organizational unit and find the Lin entry.”
The DC in DC=example means Domain Component. It does not mean Domain Controller; the abbreviations happen to coincide.
4. Base, Scope, Filter, and Attributes: four search settings
These settings are central to interpreting a search.
To inventory company accounts, specify where to start, how deeply to search, which entries to match, and which fields to return.

visual.caption: Figure 2 | Four questions in an LDAP search
visual.description: These settings jointly define the query; peer cards do not imply execution order.

items.title: 01 · Base
items.body: Where to start? For example, People.

items.title: 02 · Scope
items.body: How deep? Immediate children or all descendants.

items.title: 03 · Filter
items.body: Which entries match? For example, users only.

items.title: 04 · Attributes
items.body: Which fields? For example, name and email.

sourceBody.text: Scope has three basic values.

rows: Excludes the starting entry and deeper descendants
Search from the start through its descendants
Includes the starting entry and all descendants

sourceBody.text: This is the standard LDAP search model, also reflected in Microsoft AD query APIs.
Compare three scopes on the same directory tree

visual.caption: Figure 3 | Three search depths on the same tree
visual.description: Lines show parent-child relationships. Green outlines mark one-level candidates: Lin, Chen, and the research group, before Filter or permissions. base examines People only; subtree includes all six entries, without automatically covering other domains.

items.title: People
items.body: Search base; the only base-scope candidate

items.title: Research group
items.body: Immediate child of People, with children of its own

sourceBody.text: This reveals a common inventory error:
If a company has 500 users and a one-level search returns 20, you cannot conclude that the company has only 20. Other people may belong to deeper subdepartments.
Even subtree does not necessarily cover every domain in the company. It searches downward from the specified Base; it does not automatically cover the entire AD forest.
5. RootDSE and Global Catalog: why do query entry points differ?
Imagine a multinational company with employee systems in Taiwan, the United States, and Japan.
Asking the Taiwan administrator may not return every employee in the other two countries.
AD has a similar scope issue.
RootDSE: the server's service information sign
RootDSE is a special entry through which an LDAP server provides information about itself.
It can describe supported capabilities and directory entry points.
For example, defaultNamingContext helps identify the default domain's search base.
Reading RootDSE does not grant permission to read every employee account or provide a complete map of AD.
Global Catalog (GC): an index across domains
Think of GC as an index across domains, useful when you do not already know which domain holds a record.
Its limitation matters: for other domains, GC generally holds a subset of each object's attributes, rather than a full copy of every field.
A missing field in a GC response therefore need not mean that the original directory lacks that information.
6. LDAP Bind, permissions, and TLS: signing in does not grant universal visibility
Imagine entering an office building with an employee badge.
Passing the entrance check does not authorize entry to the executive office, server room, or finance office.
Separate three questions in LDAP as well.

rows: The authentication identity currently in use
Which objects or fields that identity can access
Whether protections such as encryption, integrity, and server authentication are established

sourceBody.text: LDAP Bind concerns the connection's authentication state. Even a successful Bind does not establish permission to read all data.
Common LDAP transport arrangements include the following.

rows: The protocol name alone does not establish encryption
Negotiate TLS on an existing LDAP connection
Use TLS from the beginning of the connection
Message integrity and authenticity for applicable non-TLS SASL sessions

sourceBody.text: LDAP Signing is not encryption.

Signing resembles protection against unnoticed document changes; encryption prevents outsiders from readily reading its contents. TLS can provide confidentiality, integrity, and server authentication, provided it is correctly established and the certificate is validated.
In Microsoft AD, LDAP Signing primarily applies to non-TLS SASL sessions. Do not treat it as an independent extra layer applied to every LDAP connection.
7. The central case: what does sizeLimitExceeded mean?
Return to the lesson's scenario.
You are authorized to query accounts in the company's People unit. The tool displays:

visual.caption: Figure 4 | LDAP Search Result: incomplete results
visual.description: Synthetic teaching data. Two entries establish only the visible results received. Code 4 indicates a size limit, not a directory containing only two people. Requesting cn alone cannot establish the absence of mail.

sourceBody.text: sizeLimitExceeded means the search hit a record limit and did not retrieve a normally completed result set.
RFC 4511 defines result codes including success = 0, timeLimitExceeded = 3, and sizeLimitExceeded = 4.
You can confirm that this query retrieved two records. The complete count remains unknown.
Because you requested only cn, the absence of an email field cannot establish that those employees have no email address.
How can you retrieve subsequent results?

Paging can help when supported by the server and permitted by the search conditions. Page size and the whole search's sizeLimit are different settings: retaining the same total limit does not make paging automatically bypass it.
Imagine a 500-page register that can be printed only 100 pages at a time. You need five batches and must verify receipt of all of them.

LDAP paging can use continuation information, called a cookie, returned by the server. Check each result status and confirm a final empty cookie before declaring the paging sequence finished. Record interruptions, errors, or lost continuation information.

visual.caption: Figure 5 | Retrieve batches and confirm completion
visual.description: Arrows indicate paging continuation, without increasing permissions or scope. A page size of 100 is illustrative. Check result codes and the final empty cookie; calculate the total from actual returned entries.

items.title: Page 1
items.body: Retrieve 100 entries and retain the server continuation cookie.

items.title: Page 2
items.body: Send the previous cookie and retrieve another batch; 100 in this example.

items.title: Subsequent pages
items.body: Check each result status until the final empty cookie.

sourceBody.text: Paging retrieves data in batches. It does not increase your permissions or expand the search scope automatically.
Also remember:
success means that this LDAP operation completed successfully. It does not establish that the company's entire account inventory is complete.
8. Why does this matter for CEH?
CEH M04 Enumeration teaches you to interpret information exposure and visibility from service responses.
Suppose an authorized enterprise assessment finds that a low-privilege account can query employee names, groups, and organizational structure.
Go beyond simply counting the returned accounts:
Was this identity intended to read that information? Does visibility exceed business needs? Are the results complete? Which data was never requested?
Defenders should record identity, server, time, Base, Scope, Filter, Attributes, result code, and paging completion, while applying least privilege to directory visibility.
Large volumes of LDAP queries alone do not establish an attack. Legitimate asset inventories and directory synchronization services can also generate many queries.
A six-question framework for judging completeness

rows: Treating a low-privilege view as the whole directory
Treating one organizational unit as an entire domain
4. What are the Filter and Attributes?
Missing other matching populations or unrequested fields
5. What are the result code and paging status?
6. Are all required directories and domains covered?
Treating one domain as the entire company

sourceBody.text: The same reasoning applies to other service enumeration, paginated APIs, database queries, and asset inventories: define the observation scope, then decide what the evidence supports.
Comprehension check | CEH M04-08
You are a commissioned security auditor inventorying enterprise AD accounts.
An authenticated low-privilege account performs this LDAP query over a valid TLS connection:
Query record

Base: OU=People,DC=example,DC=test
Scope: one-level
Attributes: cn
Result: 20 entries
Result Code: success (0)
A colleague says: “We have confirmed that People and every subdepartment contain only 20 people in total, and none has an email address.”
Answer three questions:
Q1. What is wrong with the colleague's conclusions?
Q2. Which search setting should you adjust first to include all subdepartments beneath People?
Q3. Why does success (0) still not prove that these 20 entries are the complete inventory?

paragraphs: Q1: one-level covers only immediate children of People, excluding People itself and deeper subdepartments. cn is the only requested attribute; missing mail does not establish that employees lack email addresses. The 20 entries are results visible to this identity under these query conditions, rather than a count of everyone in the unit.

Q2: First change Scope to subtree, retain the correct Base, and verify Filter, required Attributes, identity visibility, and all required directories. subtree includes the base and its descendants without automatically covering other domains.

Q3: success (0) establishes only successful completion of this operation under its specified conditions. Inventory completeness still requires checking identity, Base, Scope, Filter, Attributes, size/time limits, the final empty paging cookie, and coverage of every required directory and domain. Valid TLS protects transport without increasing read permissions.

sourceBody.text: Supplement A | What is LDAP? An introduction from first principles
Think of LDAP as a standard way of asking a company's employee directory for information.
Imagine a company with 3,000 employees, each with a computer account, password, email address, department, and permissions for different systems.
Maintaining a separate employee record in every application is difficult. When someone leaves, IT might otherwise have to delete their account from more than a dozen systems.
A centralized Directory Service addresses this management problem; LDAP is a protocol that lets other software communicate with it.
1. Start with a company scenario
Imagine a company called Kairos Technology.

visual.caption: Figure 6 | Central company employee directory
visual.description: Lines show shared use of a central directory, rather than a mandatory LDAP path for every sign-in. Systems can query it; sign-in and authorization workflows may also use Kerberos or other protocols.

items.title: Central employee directory
items.body: Accounts, names, departments, groups, and related information

sourceBody.text: An employee named Ming works there.
Ming opens an internal system and enters the account ming and a password.
The system may authenticate through the central directory using LDAP instead of storing Ming's password itself.
It can ask:

items: Does the account ming exist?
Is the user authenticated successfully?
Which department does the user belong to?
Is the user a member of an administrator group?

sourceBody.text: The directory responds according to the authentication method, permissions, and query conditions. The application then decides whether Ming may enter and which functions are available.
Accounts can thus be managed centrally rather than recreated independently in every application.
2. What does LDAP stand for?
LDAP = Lightweight Directory Access Protocol
Break the name into its parts:

rows: Simpler than earlier X.500 directory access approaches
Like an organized employee phone book
Query, read, or modify data when authorized
Shared rules followed by both parties

sourceBody.text: Keep the classification clear:
LDAP is a communication protocol, rather than a database product or an individual server.
This is its basic role in IETF RFC 4511 and Microsoft's LDAP documentation.
3. How do LDAP, Active Directory, and a Domain Controller differ?
These three names are easy to confuse.
Use a company's administrative system as an analogy.

rows: Standard language for asking HR for information
The company's personnel and account management system
The office actually providing the service

sourceBody.text: Windows Server can host Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS). Other applications can use LDAP to query its directory information.
AD also uses technologies including Kerberos, DNS, and Group Policy.
LDAP can work with directory services other than Microsoft AD, including OpenLDAP.
4. What does LDAP data look like?
Suppose the company stores Ming's record.

visual.caption: Figure 7 | Employee record: Ming
visual.description: A simplified generic LDAP Entry. Account attributes vary between directories; AD commonly uses sAMAccountName. An ou attribute does not replace the DN identifying the entry location.

sourceBody.text: A Distinguished Name (DN) identifies an entry's position in the directory.
For example:
cn=Ming,ou=People,dc=example,dc=test
Read this as:

items: cn=Ming: find the Ming entry.
ou=People: it is in the People organizational unit.
dc=example,dc=test: the domain directory is example.test.

sourceBody.text: Think of the DN as a complete address, rather than just a person's name.
5. How does an LDAP search happen?
Suppose an administrator wants to find Engineering employees.

visual.caption: Figure 8 | How an LDAP search happens
visual.description: Arrows show processing order for this search. Interpret entries together with final status; a successful response does not establish universal visibility.

items.title: 2 · Send LDAP Search
items.body: Specify search base, depth, and conditions.

items.title: 3 · Directory server
items.body: Search according to conditions and access permissions.

items.title: 4 · Return results
items.body: Ming, Hua, Mei, and others, together with search status.

sourceBody.text: LDAP Search has four basic settings:
For example, the LDAP filter:
(cn=Ming)
Finds entries whose cn equals Ming.
Another example:
(mail=*)
Finds entries with a mail attribute.
LDAP also includes operations such as Bind (establish authentication state), Modify, and Add. Whether an operation is permitted depends on server configuration and permissions.
6. Is LDAP secure, and why does CEH cover it?
LDAP alone does not establish encryption in transit, so security settings matter.

rows: Using LDAP does not by itself establish encrypted data
Negotiate TLS on the existing connection

sourceBody.text: With TLS, validate the server certificate correctly to avoid trusting an impersonating server. Microsoft also recommends appropriate TLS or SASL protection for LDAP communication.
For CEH, LDAP matters because enterprise directories can hold extensive organizational information. Incorrect permissions may expose accounts and groups to people who should not see them.
Remember:
Finding an account does not reveal its password, and successful LDAP authentication does not establish administrator privileges.
7. Review with four questions

items: What is LDAP? A communication protocol for software to access directory services.
What is it used for? Query accounts, groups, and organizational information, and support related authentication and authorization management workflows.
Is LDAP the same as AD? No. LDAP is a protocol; AD is Microsoft's directory and identity management technology.
Is LDAP secure? That depends on authentication, access permissions, and transport protection settings.

sourceBody.text: Short quiz: check your understanding
1. A company uses Active Directory for employee accounts. Which protocol can another internal system typically use to query employee data?
LDAP
HDMI
USB
2. What does finding Ming's account through LDAP establish?
You have obtained Ming's password
Matching, visible account data exists within the query scope
You have company administrator privileges
3. Which description of LDAP and Active Directory is correct?
They are identical products
LDAP is a protocol; AD is a directory management system supporting LDAP
LDAP works only on Windows

paragraphs: Question 1: LDAP. LDAP is a directory access protocol; HDMI and USB serve different interface purposes and do not establish an AD directory query.
Question 2: Matching, visible account data exists within the query scope. This neither provides the password nor grants administrator privileges.
Question 3: LDAP is a protocol; AD is a directory management system supporting LDAP. They are different things, and systems such as OpenLDAP also support LDAP.

sourceBody.text: Next, connect LDAP, Kerberos, and DNS to understand enterprise sign-in and permission management in Active Directory. This links CEH enumeration to practical Windows network engineering.
Supplement B | What is Kerberos? An introduction from first principles
Kerberos is an Authentication Protocol. It uses encrypted tickets so users do not have to enter a password again for every integrated company system they access.
Think of it as the company's central identity check and pass system.
LDAP can query the employee directory; Kerberos helps prove that someone really is the claimed employee.
Keep these roles in mind:

items: LDAP: query identity records and department information.
Kerberos: prove identity using encrypted tickets.

sourceBody.text: Both often appear in Active Directory (AD), with different responsibilities.
1. Why does a company need Kerberos?
Imagine Kairos Technology has 3,000 employees who use many systems each day.

visual.caption: Figure 9 | Must every system ask for the password again?
visual.description: Ming signs in to the company computer at 9:00 AM. The three services are peers. Appropriate Kerberos integration can reduce repeated sign-ins, while each service still checks authorization.

items.title: Employee Ming
items.body: Signs in to the company computer at 9:00 AM

sourceBody.text: If every system independently handles accounts and passwords, repeated authentication and password administration become substantial problems.

Kerberos offers another approach: at initial sign-in, prove identity to a trusted central authentication service and obtain a credential for requesting other tickets. Obtain a corresponding service ticket when accessing a particular service.
This supports Single Sign-On (SSO).
2. Understand Kerberos through amusement park passes
Imagine visiting a large amusement park.
It has a roller coaster, a pirate ship ride, and an aquarium.
Your visit involves three stages.
Stage 1: establish that you are an authorized visitor
At the entrance, staff verify your identity and issue a pass that lets you request tickets for individual attractions.
This pass resembles a Kerberos Ticket-Granting Ticket (TGT).
Stage 2: obtain a ticket for a particular attraction
To ride the roller coaster, take the pass to the ticket office and request a roller coaster ticket.
This is analogous to a Service Ticket.
Stage 3: enter the specified attraction
At the roller coaster entrance, present the dedicated ticket. Staff validate it and apply the attraction's access rules before letting you ride.
Similarly, a target service validates a Kerberos ticket and then checks access permissions.
You do not need to return to the park entrance for every identity check. However, the initial pass does not grant unrestricted entry to every attraction.
A TGT requests service tickets; a Service Ticket proves identity to a particular service.
3. How Kerberos actually works
Kerberos involves three main roles.

rows: Validates tickets and provides the service

sourceBody.text: In Windows Active Directory, the KDC usually runs on a Domain Controller (DC).
The KDC contains two logical functions: AS (Authentication Service) issues TGTs; TGS (Ticket-Granting Service) issues service tickets. They need not be separate computers.

visual.caption: Figure 10 | Three stages of Kerberos ticket use
visual.description: The first two stages show request and reply. In stage three the service checks authorization; access according to permissions is not a fixed AP reply packet. Mutual authentication can use AP_REP. AS/TGS are logical KDC functions; pre-authentication round trips, key details, and cache reuse are simplified.

items.title: Ming's computer → KDC / AS
items.body:
Stage 1 · AS Exchange
Request an initial ticket and prove identity
Receive a TGT

items.title: Ming's computer → KDC / TGS
items.body:
Stage 2 · TGS Exchange
Use the TGT to request a file-server ticket
Receive a Service Ticket

items.title: Ming's computer → File server
items.body:
Stage 3 · AP Exchange
Present the service ticket and Authenticator
After validation, access according to permissions

sourceBody.text: This is the basic Kerberos V5 design described in [IETF RFC 4120](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4120.html).
Where does encryption occur?
Kerberos does not simply hand your password to every server.
In a common password-based authentication flow:

items: Ming's computer uses a password-derived key to prove possession of the required authentication information.
After verification, the KDC issues an encrypted TGT and corresponding session-key information.
To access the file server, Ming uses the TGT to request a service ticket from the KDC.
The KDC issues an encrypted ticket that the target service can validate.
The file server checks the ticket and associated authentication information.

sourceBody.text: In the standard password-based Kerberos flow, the user's plaintext password need not be sent over the network directly to the service server.
Tickets also have validity periods, encryption protection, and authentication mechanisms that resist replay.

However, Kerberos primarily authenticates identities. It does not establish that all subsequent application data is automatically encrypted. Check the application protocol, such as HTTPS or SMB encryption, and its security settings.
4. Why does Kerberos care about computer time?
This connection matters in computer engineering and CEH.
Suppose Ming's computer shows 9:00 AM while the Domain Controller shows 9:20 AM.
Kerberos uses timestamps to help resist Replay Attacks.
With an excessive time difference, a server may reject authentication because the authentication information falls outside its accepted time window.
Typical Windows AD policy defaults allow 5 minutes of clock skew, and policy can change this tolerance.
This helps explain the importance of Network Time Protocol (NTP) and Windows time synchronization in enterprise networks.
Connect this to NTP enumeration in CEH M04: clock synchronization can directly affect authentication reliability, beyond displaying the correct time.
5. How do LDAP, Kerberos, Active Directory, and DNS work together?
A table connects their responsibilities.

rows: What information is in the directory?
Query users, groups, and other directory information
Who manages identities and directory data?
Provide domain accounts, directories, and management mechanisms

sourceBody.text: For example:

When Ming signs in to a Windows domain computer and opens a shared folder, DNS can help find domain services or the target host; Kerberos can authenticate; AD supplies relevant account and group information; the file server applies permissions to decide whether access is allowed.
LDAP may serve directory queries, but not every Windows domain sign-in requires the client to issue a direct LDAP query.
6. What Kerberos security risks matter for CEH?
Kerberos is a mature authentication protocol, but remains exposed to attacks under certain conditions.

rows: Impersonate a holder by stealing usable tickets
Protect endpoints, credentials, and ticket storage
Use certain service tickets to attempt offline guesses of weak service-account passwords
Strong passwords, gMSA, and appropriate encryption algorithms
Forge TGTs after obtaining highly sensitive Kerberos keys
Strictly protect domain controllers and KRBTGT keys

sourceBody.text: You do not need to memorize every label at once. Understand the security relationship:
Kerberos reduces repeated password transmission, but stolen endpoints, tickets, or core keys can still enable impersonation.

In Windows domain auditing, event ID 4768 helps observe TGT requests, while 4769 concerns service-ticket requests. These records help investigate authentication anomalies; a single event alone does not establish an attack.
7. Can you inspect Kerberos tickets on Windows?
Yes. In a Windows environment you are authorized to use, open PowerShell or Command Prompt:
klist
If the current logon session has Kerberos tickets, this command lists cached ticket information, including the corresponding services and validity start and end times.
An empty list does not necessarily mean Kerberos is broken. You might be using a local account, have not accessed a service requiring Kerberos, or be in a session using another authentication method.
This form of the command reads information and does not actively modify domain settings.
8. Three concepts to check your Kerberos understanding
1. After signing in, Ming wants to access a file server. What does Kerberos normally use first to request a service ticket?
TGT
LDAP search results
IP address
2. Does successful Kerberos authentication mean Ming may read every confidential company file?
Yes, authentication grants every permission
No, the target service must still check authorization
3. What can happen if a computer and its Domain Controller differ by 20 minutes?
Kerberos may reject authentication because of clock skew
LDAP automatically deletes users
All service tickets become permanently valid

paragraphs: Question 1: TGT. The client uses it to request a ticket for the specified service from the KDC's TGS. LDAP results and an IP address cannot replace it.
Question 2: No, the target service must still check authorization. Establishing identity and permitting a particular file read are separate decisions.

Question 3: Kerberos may reject authentication because of clock skew. Twenty minutes exceeds the common five-minute default, though effective policy still needs checking. It does not automatically delete LDAP users or make tickets permanently valid.

sourceBody.text: Kerberos establishes who an identity is; access to confidential information still requires the service's authorization decision.
The two ticket types, TGT and Service Ticket, also show why knowing a password, holding a ticket, and having system permissions are separate facts.
